compound.name: eriocitrin
compound.one_liner: The flavanone glycoside EMA calls the dominant phenolic of peppermint leaf: the tea compound, absent from the oil.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Mentha x piperita L., folium and aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/522409/2013 (15 Jan 2020). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/assessment-report-mentha-x-piperita-l-folium-and-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.note: Presence verified; amount null because EMA quotes 6.6-15.0 % without a confirmed denominator (possibly % of phenolic metabolites). KNApSAcK: Eriocitrin C00008295 (CAS 13463-28-0) in Mentha piperita. Not in Duke. EMA calls eriocitrin 'the dominant phenolic secondary metabolite'. | Basis as recorded: as quoted by EMA for peppermint leaf clones (denominator not captured - check the report before publishing)

processing_stability.note: As a glycoside it belongs to the leaf/tea side of the oil-versus-tea contrast; solubility values not sourced.

compound.teaching_note: Peppermint oil and peppermint tea are different chemical objects: the oil is menthol/menthone; the leaf's dominant phenolic is eriocitrin [6].
gaps: Amount null: EMA's 6.6-15.0 % figure lacks a confirmed denominator (possibly % of phenolic metabolites; check the report).
